sentences.text: If you dig a hole, fill it with water and add goldfish, you have a fish pond.
But the fish make waste that feeds algae, so the clear water turns green.
The waste turns into ammonia, and above about 0.02 mg per liter it can harm the fish's gills.
So you add a pump and a pipe to pull the dirty water out of the pond.
A settling tank lets sludge sink, scum floats on top, and clearer water goes back to the pond.
But ammonia is dissolved, so the clear-looking water carries it straight back into the pond.
So you add a bed of gravel on the return pipe, giving bacteria a place to live.
Its bacteria turn ammonia into nitrite and then nitrate, a process called nitrification.
Water flows through the gravel, the bacteria eat the ammonia, the gauge falls to zero and the pond turns clear.
Nitrifying one gram of ammonia nitrogen into nitrate uses about 4.57 grams of oxygen from the water.
But on a hot day, warm water holds less oxygen, so the bacteria and fish compete and the fish crowd the surface.
So you add an air pump that blows bubbles up through the water, and the oxygen climbs back.
Then you plant young trees behind the pond to shade it, so the water stays cool.
And the goldfish memory of three seconds is not true.
Goldfish remember things for at least three months, not three seconds.
Add rocks round the edge and lily pads on the water.
Congratulations, you have built a fish pond.
